topics.label: Lecture opening and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the main learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the study of transforming tumor viruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and the development of assays to test transforming capacity.

topics.label: Classifications and mechanisms of oncogenic and tumor-suppressor mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define how cancer gene mutations are classified and illustrate how alterations in regulators such as Rb and p53 alter cell cycle control.

topics.label: Mechanisms and forms of genetic instability in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the cellular defects in DNA repair and chromosome segregation that generate sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cumulative genetic alterations drive stepwise tumor progression and how germline mutations accelerate this pathway.

topics.label: Closing remarks and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the lecture, provides book recommendations, and previews the next topic.
